clue.text: See 5
Scrag end of mutton to take off?

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only the tail of mutton is used

parts.note: to take off someone is to mimic them, which is to ape them

explanation.surface: A butcher's question about cutting the scrag end from a joint of mutton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrag end' looks like one butcher's term, but 'Scrag' alone is the definition and 'end of' works on mutton. Scrag is the neck of mutton, and also slang for a person's neck.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrag is the neck of an animal or person, and the back of the neck has its own name.

clue.text: Originally put down, first of psychologists who finally cut it

definitions.text: Originally put down, first of psychologists who finally cut it

indicators.note: done in an original, fresh way, so the letters of put down are made into something new
cut means those two letters are taken out of the fodder before the rearrangement
the first of a word is its opening letter, here from psychologists
finally points to the last letter of the word who

explanation.surface: A note that a pioneering psychologist's idea was first written down and later trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' rearranges PUT DOWN once 'cut' has removed P (first of psychologists) and O (who finally). Wilhelm Wundt founded the first laboratory of experimental psychology, so the whole clue describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilhelm Wundt, a German scientist of the nineteenth century, is called the father of experimental psychology, the first to set it up as a science.

clue.text: Duet I'd done with leader of Pogues celebrated without one getting steamed

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: a deed celebrated in verse is sung

indicators.note: done in the sense of done over, beaten up, so the letters are knocked into a new order
the leader of a word is its first letter, from Pogues

explanation.surface: A duet sung with the Pogues' frontman, celebrated except by someone who got drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steamed' looks like slang for drunk, but here it is cooking. 'done' rearranges DUET I'D plus P (leader of Pogues) into UETPUDDI, which sits 'without', inside, SUNG. A suet pudding is a heavy British dessert made with beef fat.
explanation.definitionFit: A suet pudding is traditionally cooked by steaming it in a basin for hours, so it is a dish that gets steamed.

clue.text: With 1A dating from 1752, noisily steps over 31

indicators.note: noisily means we go by how a word is said out loud, not its spelling

parts.note: a stile is a set of steps for climbing over a wall, and 31 across is a wall

explanation.surface: A puzzling note about loud footsteps over a wall, dated to the eighteenth century.
explanation.walkthrough: 31 is STONEWALL, so 'steps over 31' are a stile. New Style dates are those of the Gregorian calendar, which Britain adopted in 1752.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain switched to the Gregorian calendar in 1752, and dates under that reform are called New Style.

clue.text: Tips disregarded in the most influential decade

indicators.note: the tips are the two end letters, which are left off

parts.note: the weightiest matters carry the most influence

explanation.surface: Someone says the most influential decade ignored advice or gratuities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips' looks like gratuities or advice; here it is the end letters of WEIGHTIEST, which 'disregarded' removes.
explanation.definitionFit: The years 1980 to 1989, or any years ending 80 to 89, form a ten-year span named after the number.

clue.text: Star stirring up a platelayer with cracks I ignored

indicators.note: stirring mixes these letters up into a new order
cracks means breaks into, so one piece is opened and another put inside
ignored means the letter I is left out

parts.note: a lineman is a railway worker who lays and maintains track, as a platelayer does

explanation.surface: A celebrity rouses a railway worker, telling cracks but ignoring something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirring' rearranges UP A into PAU. 'I ignored' takes I from LINEMAN to give LNEMAN, which W (with) 'cracks' to make LNEWMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The actor of Cool Hand Luke and The Sting was one of Hollywood's biggest film stars.

clue.text: Comic stand-in so harsh!

indicators.note: comic means funny or absurd, so these letters are jumbled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A complaint that a comedian's replacement was too cruel.
explanation.definitionFit: Music that is harsh to the ear is discordant, its notes clashing rather than blending.

clue.text: Nimrod's second last to offer up terminal sacrifices

parts.note: the setter Nimrod speaking of himself says I'm, short for I am
a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: to offer up is to give up, so the final letter of the word is surrendered

parts.note: the last news is the latest

explanation.surface: The setter says he's second to last in offering a final sacrifice.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by name, so 'Nimrod's' means 'I am'. 'second last' looks like one phrase but splits into two words, and 'to offer up terminal' gives up the final letter of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To immolate is to kill as a sacrifice, especially by burning, so it is the verb for offering up victims.

clue.text: 34 did a runner from corn store

definitions.note: 34 across is a man; a man's first name stands for a man

indicators.note: something that runs from a place leaves it, so those letters come out

parts.note: a granary is a store for grain
did a runner is slang for ran away

explanation.surface: A man fled from a grain store.
explanation.walkthrough: 34 across is MAN, and the definition is a man's first name standing for any man.
explanation.definitionFit: A common male first name is an example of a man, the meaning of 34 across.

clue.text: Perhaps resembling Quaker coin, decimal with 1A

definitions.note: the new penny was the coin of British decimal currency from 1971

parts.note: William Penn was a leading Quaker who founded Pennsylvania
the suffix -y means having the quality of, resembling

explanation.surface: Talk of a Quaker-like coin in decimal money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' says Penn is one example of a Quaker. Britain switched to decimal money in 1971, and the coins were first called new pence.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's decimal penny, a hundredth of a pound, was first named the new penny in 1971.

clue.text: County set left after broadcast got more and more revolting

indicators.note: after places the county part behind the broadcast word
broadcast means spoken on air, so the sound of a word is used rather than its spelling

parts.note: someone who got more, increased, grew

indicators.note: left in the sense of departed, so the set letters go

parts.note: Somerset is a county in south-west England

explanation.surface: A county set left after an announcement that grew increasingly disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'County set' looks like the gentry; it is SOMERSET with 'set left'. 'more and more' hides the definition as 'more revolting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gruesome is horrible or revolting, and the comparative form means more horrible.

clue.text: What's adolescent, having left to cross river, ringing in?

definitions.text: What's adolescent, having left to cross river, ringing in?

indicators.note: having means holding, so the adolescent word contains everything that follows

parts.note: a teen is an adolescent

indicators.note: to cross is to span, so the word for leaving straddles the river

parts.note: someone who left went

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the river surrounds the little word in

parts.note: the Tyne is a river in north-east England, through Newcastle

explanation.surface: A riddle about a teenager who left to cross a river, ringing in something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing', 'to cross' and 'having' each wrap one piece round the next, three levels deep. The puzzle appeared on New Year's Day 2019, so the clue also names the year being rung in.
explanation.definitionFit: On 1 January 2019 bells were ringing in the new year, so the whole clue describes that year as the one arriving.

clue.text: Slash Mini in Glasgow?

definitions.meaning: slash is British slang for urinating, as is the word for answering a call of nature
in Scots speech small or tiny is said with this word, so it describes something mini

explanation.surface: Cut a small car in a Scottish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one spelling: a childish word for urine, and the Scottish word for little.

clue.text: Promise broken by Ludwig's first Symphony with 1A

indicators.note: a word broken by a letter has that letter pushed into it

parts.note: to give your word is to promise

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the name Ludwig

explanation.surface: A broken promise over Beethoven's first symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ludwig's first Symphony' suggests Beethoven, but the symphony is Dvorak's, and 'Ludwig's first' gives only L.
explanation.definitionFit: Dvorak's ninth symphony, written in America, is known as From the New World.

clue.text: View of ocean gleaming

indicators.note: of here means taken from within these two words, the letters running across the gap

explanation.surface: A seascape of shining water.
explanation.definitionFit: A view or standpoint on an issue is an angle, a way of looking at it.

clue.text: Not at first supporting the German plan to reorganise Europe with 1A

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: someone supporting a cause is for it
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A German plan to remake Europe that was not supported at first.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Order was the Nazi scheme to reshape conquered Europe under German rule.

clue.text: See 11
Such a claim covering today's first light with respect to yesterday's?

parts.note: 1 across, the first entry in today's grid, is the word meaning fresh
for can mean with respect to, as in 'so much for that'
yesterday's things are aged, past their best

explanation.surface: An insurance claim covering today's first light, in place of yesterday's.
explanation.walkthrough: The previous day's Independent puzzle by Eimi used the same grid and a similar theme, so this one replaces it. 'covering' just joins the insurance picture to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A replacement insurance policy pays out for brand-new goods in place of worn ones; such a claim is named for that swap.

clue.text: Offensive male sex organ parts — with 1A where is Mark?

indicators.note: parts means splits apart, so one word is opened for the other

parts.note: the Tet Offensive was a 1968 attack in the Vietnam War
the stamen is the male reproductive part of a flower

explanation.surface: A crude remark about a male organ, followed by a question about someone called Mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' looks like an adjective; it is the noun, the Tet Offensive. 'Mark' is the Gospel of Mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gospel of Mark is one of the books of the Christian scriptures after the Gospels begin, the New Testament.

clue.text: Daisy on back of tandem that with 1A Jacky may have in nursery

definitions.text: that with 1A Jacky may have in nursery

indicators.note: on means placed after, the flower following the letter
the back of a word is its last letter, from tandem

parts.note: the Michaelmas daisy is a kind of aster

explanation.surface: A girl called Daisy riding on the back of a tandem bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daisy' looks like a girl's name; it is a flower. The nursery rhyme 'See Saw Margery Daw' says 'Jacky shall have a new master'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme the boy Jacky gets a new employer, a new boss.

clue.text: Historical action court cases drastically alter

indicators.note: cases means encloses, so the courting word holds the other letters

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: drastically means changed radically, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Legal cases changing the record of a historic event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court cases' looks like lawsuits; 'court' is WOO and 'cases' holds ATERL, from 'alter' rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1815 battle in Belgium where Napoleon was finally defeated is a famous military engagement.

clue.text: Lecturer's advice to young man? It's not good, and extremely vulgar

parts.note: L is an abbreviation for lecturer

indicators.note: not means the letter is excluded

parts.note: 'Go west, young man' is a famous American saying urging settlement of the frontier

explanation.surface: A lecturer tells a young man something is bad and crude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go west, young man' is an American phrase from the frontier era. Removing G leaves OWEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The most base or coarse behaviour is at the bottom of the scale, so the lowest is the most vulgar.

clue.text: At best crude promo is in this?

definitions.text: At best crude promo is in this?

indicators.note: is in puts one piece inside the other
crude means rough and unfinished, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: a promo is an advert, an ad

explanation.surface: A question whether a crude advert is offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crude' rearranges AT BEST into BTASTE, and AD goes in after B. The whole clue says a crude advert is in poor taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crude and offensive is in poor taste, lacking decorum.

clue.text: Perhaps a rising trend of the 4 with 1A

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, signals an instance, as perhaps does

explanation.surface: A trend that may be growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 is EIGHTIES. The New Age movement of alternative spirituality flourished in that decade.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Age movement of crystals and alternative spiritual beliefs was a fashion of the 1980s.

clue.text: With 1A a freedom fighter got round mum

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to have won something is to have got it
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A freedom fighter had a mother captured.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Woman was the late nineteenth century term for a woman fighting for independence and rights.

clue.text: Easy joint?

parts.note: a joint suggests a cannabis cigarette, an easy, relaxed smoke

explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' could be a hinge or carpentry; it is a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannabis cigarette is commonly known as this slang term.

clue.text: With 1A, TV talent show following fine performers

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
aces are excellent performers

explanation.surface: A TV contest following up talented acts.
explanation.walkthrough: New Faces was a British TV talent show of the 1970s and 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: New Faces was a British television talent contest that launched comedians and singers.

clue.text: Discharge explosive spirit bottles

indicators.note: bottles means holds inside, so the spirit contains the other piece

parts.note: rum is a spirit
HE stands for high explosive

explanation.surface: Explosive spirit, the sort that might discharge from bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' looks like firing; it is a mucous discharge.
explanation.definitionFit: A watery fluid flowing from the eyes or nose is a bodily discharge.

clue.text: With 1A he'll need different login from you server supplies

indicators.note: the words supply letters from inside them, spanning the gap

explanation.surface: A server warning that a newcomer needs another login.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone joining a computer system for the first time needs their own account, so a new user gets a login.

clue.text: One's forgotten to postpone 60s cinematic movement with 1A

indicators.note: forgotten means it is left out

parts.note: to waive is to put aside or defer
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is is

explanation.surface: Someone forgot to delay a film movement of the 1960s.
explanation.walkthrough: The New Wave was the French film movement of Godard and Truffaut.
explanation.definitionFit: The French New Wave, the nouvelle vague, was an influential 1960s film movement.

clue.text: 100 women kept in Milton Keynes, say, with 1A

indicators.note: kept in means held inside the other piece

parts.note: a ton is slang for a hundred

explanation.surface: A hundred women held in a planned English settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: Milton Keynes is a planned English settlement designated in 1967.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton Keynes is an example of a postwar British planned settlement, built from scratch.

clue.text: Was proudly erect after replacing centrepiece with 1A block

indicators.note: the central letters are swapped for the other piece

parts.note: someone who stood tall was proudly upright
1 across is a light in this puzzle meaning fresh

explanation.surface: A figure who stood proud after its centrepiece was replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle three letters ODT are swapped out. To stonewall is to block, as a batsman does in cricket or a politician questioners.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonewalling is obstruction, deliberately blocking progress or answers.

clue.text: I believe first of clues needs rewrite

definitions.note: the Latin word means I believe, a statement of faith

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: to rewrite something is to redo it

explanation.surface: A solver thinks the first clue needs rewriting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for I believe is used in English for a set of beliefs.

clue.text: Free excesses of air go illegally round America

parts.note: to rid is to free
the ether is the upper air
ODs, overdoses, are excesses

explanation.surface: Liberating overdoses of air while travelling illicitly around the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: To ride the rods is American slang for hoboes stealing rides under freight trains.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoboes rode beneath freight cars on the rods, travelling the country without paying.

clue.text: See 5
